subject: [PATCH] mm: mglru: splice all generations when reparenting a memcg

reviews.author: Barry Song
reviews.summary:
Reviewer Barry Song noted that Kairui's previous patch (mm/mglru: reparent folios from all generations) already implemented the same code, and Shakeel's patch makes it necessary to make this change even earlier.

Reviewer Barry Song pointed out that the patch description does not clearly explain why moving all generations is necessary, and requested a more detailed explanation.
sentiment_signals: lack of clarity in patch description
reviews.raw_body:
Thanks very much, Shakeel! I saw Kairui has exactly the same code here:

[PATCH v4 14/17] mm/mglru: reparent folios from all generations
https://lore.kernel.org/linux-mm/20261016-mglru-fg-v4-14-2106750c0bfa@tencent.com/

somehow, Shakeel's patch makes us need the change earlier even before
mglru-fg lands?

---

Thanks,
Barry

reviews.author: Kairui Song
reviews.summary:
Reviewer noted that FG's folio_inc_lru_refs may cause a race between aging and lazy promotion, potentially landing a folio in a stall gen list, but agreed that this issue is not critical and can be addressed separately.

Reviewer Kairui Song agrees that the patch improves safety and cleanliness of the code
reviews.raw_body:
Thanks for looking into this!

FG needed that because FG's folio_inc_lru_refs is a generic MGLRU
lockless lazy promotion, it may cause race between aging & lazy
promotion, landing a folio in a stall gen list. This isn't a big
problem, the worst outcome is a hotness inversion, which happens
almost once in a million times.

And right as Shakeel pointed out the problem already exists for
reparenting and lazy promotion, so we can fix it first.

---

Landing this one first is totally fine by me. The code is actually
safer and cleaner, in my opinion, with this patch.

2026-11-11.patch_summary: This patch fixes a list_del corruption issue in the Linux kernel's memory management system (mm) by splicing all generations of MGLRU lists when reparenting a memcg (memory control group). The problem occurs when a memcg goes offline and its MGLRU lists are moved to the parent, but only certain generations are moved. This can lead to a folio being left on a freed memcg, causing a use-after-free error. To fix this, the patch moves all MAX_NR_GENS lists, not just those from min_seq to max_seq, ensuring that all folios are properly reparented and avoiding the corruption issue.

reviews.author: Kairui Song
reviews.summary:
Reviewer Kairui Song pointed out that the description of sort_folio() behavior in the patch is inaccurate, as MAX_NR_GENS - MIN_NR_GENS equals 2, and a stale gen can be outside the range [min_seq, max_seq].

Reviewer Kairui Song noted that this patch is similar to a previous commit for MGLRU-FG, which is a clean fix, but was surprised the problem was already reproducible.
reviews.raw_body:
"sort_folio() puts the folio on the list for max_seq + 1" seems not
very accurate as MAX_NR_GENS - MIN_NR_GENS == 2, could be any stale
gen outside [min_seq, max_seq], right?

The fix itself looks good.

---

As Barry mentioned this is basically the same code as a prepare commit
for MGLRU-FG, which is a fine and clean fix, I just didn't realize the
problem was already reproducible though.

Thanks!

Reviewed-by: Kairui Song <kasong@tencent.com>

reviews.author: Baolin Wang
reviews.summary: The reviewer found the patch comments unclear but agreed that the proposed solution fixes a problem where a folio's generation can fall outside its LRU vector range, causing it to be left behind on a freed memcg.
reviews.raw_body:
+1. The comments are not easy to understand. IIUC, the problem is that 
the folio's gen can fall outside lruvec->[min_seq, max_seq], potentially 
causing the folio to be left behind on a memcg that is about to be freed.

But, yes, the fix is correct. So,
Reviewed-by: Baolin Wang <baolin.wang@linux.alibaba.com>
